why_how.text: School and charter buses, hired-ride drivers, and placarded hazmat haulers must halt fifteen to fifty feet before the rails, then cross; an officer's or signal's order to proceed and a posted EXEMPT sign both excuse the stop.

Before crossing railway tracks, school buses, charter buses, drivers transporting paying passengers and vehicles required to display hazardous-material placards must halt fifteen to fifty feet from the tracks. This stop is unnecessary when a police officer or highway traffic signal directs traffic onward, or when an EXEMPT sign marks the crossing.

Stalled on the tracks with a train near, keep cranking the starter until the train shows, stand clear waving at the engineer, then get everyone out at once and walk clear of the rails at a forty-five-degree angle toward the oncoming train.

Stuck or stalled at a crossing, empty the vehicle and run far even with no train in sight, then phone the blue-and-white ENS sign's number with its crossing ID, or call emergency services at nine-one-one when no sign stands.
A stall with a train in view adds restart attempts and engineer-waving to the evacuation, while a stall with no train in view goes straight to evacuation plus the ENS call.

School and charter buses, hired-ride drivers, and placarded hazmat haulers must halt fifteen to fifty feet before the rails, then cross; an officer's or signal's order to proceed and a posted EXEMPT sign both excuse the stop. Before crossing railway tracks, school buses, charter buses, drivers transporting paying passengers and vehicles required to display hazardous-material placards must halt fifteen to fifty feet from the tracks. This stop is unnecessary when a police officer or highway traffic signal directs traffic onward, or when an EXEMPT sign marks the crossing. Stalled on the tracks with a train near, keep cranking the starter until the train shows, stand clear waving at the engineer, then get everyone out at once and walk clear of the rails at a forty-five-degree angle toward the oncoming train.
